physical_harm: Injuries on the deceased's head caused by the spade
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the circumstantial evidence, including the last seen theory, extra-judicial confession made by the accused, and the recovery of the weapon (spade) stained with human blood.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that their testimony, while having minor improvements and contradictions, did not undermine the prosecution's case. The court found the testimony of PW14 and others to be reliable and not tainted.
post_offence_conduct: Accused 'BS' absconded, and the appellant along with accused 'J' came to PW8 and confessed, leading to the recovery of the weapon.
trial_duration: The trial judgment was passed on 23.11.2005, the High Court affirmed the conviction on 23.11.2005, and the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal on 23.11.2005.
legal_representation: Nikhil Goel, Marsook Bafaki (for Sheela Goel) for the Appellant; Jayant K. Sud, AAG, Kuldip Singh for the Respondent.
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed

appeal_history.high_court: Affirmed the conviction and confirmed the sentence

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased was last seen with the accused persons, the appellant made a voluntary extra-judicial confession, the weapon used in the crime was recovered based on the appellant's disclosure statement, and the post-mortem report confirmed the weapon caused the injuries. The prosecution claimed these circumstances proved the accused's guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
defence_argument: The defence challenged the reliability of the 'last seen' theory, the credibility of the extra-judicial confession made after 18 days, the discrepancy in the recovery of the weapon, and the lack of corroboration of the blood group match, arguing these factors made the case vulnerable.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that circumstantial evidence can establish guilt beyond reasonable doubt if it forms a complete chain of circumstances pointing to the accused's guilt, and that extra-judicial confession, if true and voluntary, can be relied upon for conviction.
precedent_relied_upon: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra AIR 1984 SC 1622; Padala Veera Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh and others 1989 Supp (2) SCC 706; Ramreddy Rajesh Khanna Reddy and another v. State of A.P. (2006) 10 SCC 172; Gura Singh v. State of Rajasthan (2001) 2 SCC 205; Sahadevan & Another v. State of Tamil Nadu 2012 AIR sew 3206; John Pandian v. State Represented by Inspector of Police, Tamil Nadu (2010) 14 SCC 129
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the prosecution proved the case beyond reasonable doubt, and the circumstances singularly pointed to the guilt of the accused persons.
